decisions.reason: As a height-adjustable desk system it extends a core office category with functionality the firm can absorb through its existing workplace, engineering and design capabilities, and its continuation through 2019 suggests enough early signal to keep refining rather than exit.

A chair family is very close to the firm's established knowledge base in premium seating, materials and designer collaboration, so absorptive capacity is high and the product is likely to stay as part of the broad interior offer.

Floor cushions are somewhat more niche, but they still build on the firm's material and interior-solution capabilities, so management would more likely keep them as a complementary line while monitoring demand.

A soft upholstered sofa sits near the firm's core living and lounge competences, and with strong related knowledge in upholstery, quality testing and design the firm is well placed to learn and improve it commercially.
The high standing table fits the firm's direction toward flexible workplace settings and draws on familiar table and contract-furniture know-how, making retention more likely than withdrawal.

The rug collection is the riskiest because it is more distant from the firm's traditional furniture base, but as a declared flagship tied to a broader interior strategy and supported by material expertise, management would likely give it more time to build absorptive learning before dropping it.
